title: Super law rule summary — Pension standards, minimum drawdowns & transfer balance cap (FY2026-27)
summary: Rules for starting and running a Caldova Pension (account-based pension): who can start one, the minimum annual payment by age, pro-rating in the first year, rounding, the general transfer balance cap of $2.1 million for 2026-27, transfer balance credits and debits, reversionary pensions and how pension payments are taxed. Used by Benefits & Eligibility, Investment Solutions and Payments when commencing or reviewing a pension.
rules:
Commencement: an account-based pension can start once a condition of release with no cashing restriction is met (e.g. retirement after preservation age, or age 65); a transition-to-retirement (TTR) income stream can start from preservation age (60) while still working. The amount is fixed at commencement — later contributions or rollovers need a new pension.
Minimum annual payment (percentage of the balance at commencement, or at 1 July in later years, by age on that date): under 65 — 4%; 65–74 — 5%; 75–79 — 6%; 80–84 — 7%; 85–89 — 9%; 90–94 — 11%; 95 and over — 14%.
First year: the minimum is pro-rated by the days from the commencement day to 30 June (inclusive) divided by the days in the financial year. No minimum applies if the pension starts on or after 1 June.
Rounding: the minimum is rounded to the nearest $10.
Maximum: none for account-based pensions; TTR income streams are limited to 10% of the balance each year.
The minimum must be paid in full each financial year, otherwise the income stream is treated as having stopped for tax purposes.
Transfer balance cap (TBC): the general cap is $2.1 million for 2026-27 (it was $2.0 million in 2025-26). A member's personal cap is set when they first have a transfer balance account. A credit arises when a retirement-phase pension starts (its value at commencement). Regular pension payments do not reduce the account; commutations (lump sums taken out of the pension) create debits. Amounts above the cap must be commuted and attract excess transfer balance tax. The unused percentage of a member's cap drives proportional indexation of their personal cap. When a pension reverts to a spouse, the spouse's transfer balance credit arises 12 months after the death. Caldova reports transfer balance credits and debits to the ATO.
Tax: pension payments and lump sums to members aged 60 or over from a taxed fund are tax-free with no PAYG withheld. Earnings on assets supporting a retirement-phase pension are tax-exempt; TTR earnings are taxed at up to 15%. Division 296 may apply separately to members with total super balances above $3 million.
limits: A pension cannot be started with preserved money unless a relevant condition of release has been met (TTR excepted). Amounts above the member's available cap space must stay in accumulation, where earnings are taxed at up to 15%. A reversionary beneficiary must be nominated when the pension starts — Caldova accepts a spouse or de facto partner, or a child eligible for a death benefit pension (under 18; under 25 and financially dependent; or with a disability). Minimum payments cannot be deferred to a later year.
evidenceRequired: Signed Caldova Pension application (amount, income amount and frequency, nominated bank account)
Evidence of a condition of release (age 65+ needs proof of age only; ages 60–64 need a retirement declaration)
Reversionary nomination and relationship details (if any)
Investment instruction, including a cash reserve for pension payments
Transfer balance account history — any earlier retirement-phase income streams
